NDT software in Minneapolis-St. Paul: refineries, utilities, pipelines and cold weather

The Twin Cities have more heavy industry than people outside Minnesota expect. Flint Hills Resources' Pine Bend refinery in Rosemount is one of the largest refineries in the northern United States, and Marathon operates the St. Paul Park refinery on the Mississippi. Xcel Energy is headquartered in Minneapolis and runs the Prairie Island and Monticello nuclear plants along with the Sherco generating station. Enbridge's mainline and Line 3 cross northern Minnesota toward Superior, Wisconsin. Cargill and General Mills anchor a large food and agricultural processing base with boilers, pressure vessels and storage everywhere, 3M and a strong medical device sector run precision manufacturing, and the taconite plants of the Iron Range generate steady mechanical and weld inspection. Wind farms across the state add tower and structural work.

The typical Twin Cities NDT contractor lives by turnaround season. Spring and autumn refinery and utility outages pull every available technician and often bring in travellers, while winter work continues under conditions that affect how MT, PT and UT are performed. Regulators shape the work: the Minnesota Department of Health radioactive materials program for radiography licensing (Minnesota is an NRC Agreement State), the NRC at the nuclear plants, PHMSA and the Minnesota Office of Pipeline Safety for pipeline operators, and the Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry for boilers and pressure vessels. Surge staffing and certification control are where software earns its keep here.

ERP for NDT companies in Minneapolis: the short answer

The Atlantis ERP solution is a fully customized ERP for NDT and inspection companies, set up and supported by Atlantis NDT, whose founder Anoop Rayavarapu is an ASNT NDT Level III. It runs quotes, jobs, technicians, equipment, reports and invoices in one system, configured around the turnaround-driven rhythm of Twin Cities work. It is affordable, accessible and fully customizable, with pricing on request.

What changes day to day: when a refinery turnaround starts, you already know who is available, whose certifications are current, which instruments are calibrated and which truck carries the source. When the turnaround ends, the timesheets, equipment days and consumables are already on the job, ready to invoice. You are not reconciling three spreadsheets and a stack of paper timesheets in November. Each capability is a separate app, listed on the ERP apps page. The sections below apply the key apps to Minneapolis-area work.

Crew dispatch and scheduling software for Twin Cities turnarounds

Team Assignments runs every job through planned, dispatched, in field, submitted and closed, with site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates. It blocks double-booking of technicians and of equipment serial numbers, which is the first thing to break when Pine Bend, St. Paul Park and a utility outage overlap.

The technician availability calendar shows assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable, and overlaps are blocked rather than discovered on site. Approved Time Off feeds the same calendar. Each technician shows current assignment, utilisation percentage and next available date, so you can see before a turnaround who is fully booked and where the gaps are that need travelling technicians. Calendar view works for planning the season, kanban for the dispatcher moving jobs through status, and list view for the owner reviewing utilisation.

Mobilisation and demobilisation dates matter for surge crews coming in from out of state, because they drive travel, per diem and hotel costs that you will want to re-bill through the Expenses app. The Fleet app records vehicle purpose, whether a vehicle can carry radioactive sources, the transport licence number and expiry, and assignment to project and driver with dates and mileage. For radiography crews working the refineries south of the river, that keeps the source vehicle on the right job record.

Technician certification tracking software for refinery and nuclear work

The Certificates app records every technician's certifications by scheme, level and method, and computes status automatically as active, expiring soon (90 days), expired or revoked. When a turnaround brings in travellers, their certifications go into the same register as your permanent staff, so nobody is sent to a unit under a lapsed cert.

Built-in schemes are SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN and CSWIP, plus other. Each record carries the level from trainee to Level III, method, certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, industry sector, OJT hours, training hours, exam results and attachments. Examination sheets store general, specific and practical scores against a passing score that defaults to 70 percent. Certificate templates per scheme define validity in months, whether a vision test or exam is required, and minimum OJT and training hours, which helps a Level III check a traveller against your written practice quickly.

Vision tests record near vision at Jaeger J1 or J2, far vision, colour perception, contrast, examiner, clinic and expiry. The employee profile adds radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry, which nuclear site access at Prairie Island or Monticello will ask for. Daily checks create warning tasks 90 days before expiry, email alerts go to the recipients you set, and timesheets warn if work is logged without a valid certificate. The ERP records; your Level III decides qualification.

Calibration management software for equipment through a Minnesota winter

Asset Management tracks each flaw detector, phased array unit, thickness gauge, yoke, probe and source-related item by serial number with calibration frequency and status. Team Assignments warns when an out-of-calibration item is assigned, so an instrument that came back from the lab late does not quietly go out on a turnaround.

Each item records equipment type, asset tag, firmware, accessories, assigned person, condition and lifecycle: new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired or disposed. Rental rates can be recorded when you rent in extra PAUT or TOFD units for a turnaround or rent your own out in the quiet months. Calibration records hold provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag, result and next due date. The certificate register stores lab accreditation number, PDF and a valid, expiring or expired status with alerts, and Purchase can type vendors as OEM, dealer or calibration lab and tie purchase lines to a specific serial.

Cold is hard on cables, batteries and screens. The maintenance log records preventive and corrective work, repairs, cleaning, firmware updates and probe replacements with condition before and after, and issue and return records condition both ways with supervisor and manager approval. Consumables such as couplant, penetrant, developer and particles carry reorder levels and low-stock flags, so you are not short on cold-weather couplant in January.

NDT reporting software for refinery, utility and plant work

The NDT Reports app provides 17 report types with separate numbering: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday and coating, and computed radiography. A turnaround at a Twin Cities refinery can use most of them in a week, from IRIS on exchanger bundles to PMI on alloy piping and PWHT and hardness after repairs.

Method-specific fields are built in: UT with a probe calibration table; RT with source, technique, IQI type and placement; MT technique and particle type; PT method and developer; PAUT focal laws; MFL scan mode and item lines; UT thickness readings by direction; and weld or job lines with defect type and orientation, each closing as acceptable, not acceptable or acceptable with remarks. References include work order, request, WPS, contract, drawing numbers, procedure and standard.

Reports move through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures and a third-party or authorized inspector name and signature. Versioned templates in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML carry your logo; a refinery's own Excel format is filled by mapping fields to cells. The offline field app works inside units and tank farms with poor signal, stores drafts and photos and syncs later. See also Digital Twin Reporting Software.

Procedure control, including cold-weather limits

The Procedures app keeps a controlled register with document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard such as ASME Section V, acceptance criteria and the text or file. Approved revisions are locked and each revision keeps a snapshot. In Minnesota the scope and body of a PT, MT or UT procedure often need to address temperature limits, and the register keeps the approved revision in front of the technician.

The workflow runs draft, submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejected and archived states, and records who prepared, reviewed and approved each revision and when. Rejections carry a reason, and approvers receive email notifications and reminders, which helps when a client asks for a procedure revision the week before a turnaround.

An AI-assisted first draft generates a starting procedure from method, material and standard, falling back to a built-in template. A Level III still reviews, edits and approves before publication. NCR and CAPA workflows can be configured during implementation for clients whose quality programs expect nonconformances tracked to closure.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Minneapolis contracts

Quotations carry job type, site, project dates and applicable codes, with services flagged by method and category, a branded PDF and online acceptance and signature that converts to a sales order. Invoices draw on timesheets, equipment and consumables already recorded on the job.

Turnaround billing is where contractors lose money to paperwork: overtime, night shift, standby waiting for a permit, equipment days and consumables across dozens of technicians. The invoice header records NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector, with labour, equipment and consumables subtotals. Lines carry cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type and days or hours. Timesheets record work type (inspection, travel, standby, setup), billable flag and a rate multiplier, and they can be approved before they reach the invoice.

The financial dashboard shows revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA, outstanding invoices, bills and expenses over 12 months, which makes the gap between a busy spring and a quiet summer visible early. Taxes are configured during implementation, and the open REST API connects to QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation.

Winning more Twin Cities work: CRM and dashboards

The CRM records service line, lead source, NDT service type, industry sector, site country, and estimated technicians and days, and scores leads 0 to 100 as hot, warm, nurture or cold. For a contractor filling the months between turnarounds, that points the sales effort at food plants, fabricators and utilities that buy year-round.

Import leads from CSV, preview AI-personalised emails and enrol leads in drip sequences by service line. The Business Cards feature turns a photographed card into a CRM lead in one click. Dashboards show calibration due and overdue, certificates expiring and expired, and issued equipment overdue for return, next to the financial dashboard.

Implementing the Atlantis ERP in Minneapolis

Atlantis NDT implements remotely, scheduled around Central time, and plans the rollout for a quieter period so it is live before the next turnaround.

  1. Discovery. We map your service lines, turnaround calendar, methods, report formats and dispatch.
  2. Data load. Technicians, certificates, vision tests, instruments, calibration history, clients and open jobs come from your spreadsheets.
  3. Configuration. Templates, numbering, procedure register, quote and invoice layouts, alerts and integrations are set up.
  4. Pilot. A real job runs end to end, quote to invoice.
  5. Go live and support. The team moves over, with Atlantis available for adjustments before the season peaks.

Anything not built in is configured during implementation. For trainees, the eLearning portal and the Practical NDT 3D simulator can be added, and Atlantis offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training.

If your Twin Cities NDT company runs turnarounds on spreadsheets and goodwill, the Atlantis ERP gives you one system built for inspection work. It is affordable, accessible and fully customizable, suitable for small NDT companies and for larger contractors, with pricing on request.

Bring last season's turnaround and we will show you how it would have run. Book a Minneapolis ERP demo or request a quote for your Minneapolis inspection company. For plant owners, Atlantis Digital Twins places inspection data, indication maps and thickness trends on a 3D model.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT software for turnaround contractors in Minneapolis?

The best fit handles dispatch, certifications, calibration, reports and billing together. The Atlantis ERP does this and is configured to your turnaround workflow during implementation.

Can we add travelling technicians for a single turnaround?

Yes. Add them as employees with their certificates and vision tests, and they appear in availability and dispatch like permanent staff.

Does it track rented-in equipment?

Yes. Instruments carry lifecycle status including rented out, rental rates can be recorded, and calibration applies to every serial.

Is it right for a small NDT company?

Yes. You switch on only the apps you need. Pricing is quote on request.

Can it connect to our accounting software?

Yes. The open REST API integrates with QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo and other systems that accept API connections, scoped per implementation.

Does the ERP plan inspection intervals for refinery equipment?

No. The Atlantis ERP runs your NDT business and reporting; it does not calculate inspection intervals or corrosion rates.
